Subject: URGENT: HelioHealth live-stream timeouts — need warroom

Team — HelioHealth (DH-47821) reporting a sudden spike in streaming 5xxs and long silent windows on WebSocket/chunked responses. Log set attached from customer. Exec-level pressure on their side.

Quick summary from customer: 11% streaming error rate (was 0.6%), observed 20–40s silent windows followed by 502/504. All traffic appears to be via us-west-2. No obvious traffic surge from their side.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra team check ingress NLB health and proxy timeout metrics for us-west-2 (tcp timeouts, NGINX/gateway 504 origins)?
- Runtime/serving: check core inference pool (KV cache thrash, batch size changes, OOMs), and any recent kernel or quantization rollouts in the last 48 hours.
- Support: prepare a mitigation playbook (scale pools, temporarily route to steady-state non-streaming endpoint, short client retry guidance).
- Sales/CS: coordinate an incident call with Helio for T+15. They want a triage call and a plan.

Attaching their logs and my notes. Marking this P0.

Thanks — Monica
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: HelioHealth live-stream timeouts — need warroom

Quick triage (initial):
- Observed: latency/5xx spike correlates with increased timeouts at the edge (nginx/gateway) between 08:40–09:10 PDT. Several upstream connections to serving pods returned 504.
- Metrics: connection_close_counts + proxy_read_timeouts both hit 5x baseline for the customer route. No cluster-wide OOM events.
- Possible causes: transient connection backlog at the gateway (slow downstream reads), KV-cache heavy misses leading to longer token-generation blocking, and a recent autoscaler policy tweak for the dedicated pool (reduced burst nodes at night).

Immediate mitigations I can enact now (need green light):
1) Increase proxy_read_timeout and keepalive settings on the us-west-2 gateway for the Helio route (10 min -> 15 min) for 30 minutes.
2) Add two temporary inference instances (hot spare) to the dedicated pool serving DH-47821 and bump max concurrency to reduce per-request queuing.
3) Add a customer-side advisory: if client sees >10s silence, reconnect and use the polling endpoint as a fallback — I'll draft a one-paragraph note.

I will also open INF-9213 in Jira and attach the logs (link below). I recommend we not change model kernels mid-incident; avoid risky deploys.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-triage summary: HelioHealth incident (actions & exec ask)

Summary of the morning incident (for exec sync):
- Timeline: first customer report 09:12 PDT. War room at 10:20. Temporary mitigations applied by 10:30 (gateway timeouts increased + 2 hot spares added). Error rate dropped from ~11% to ~1.2% within 18 minutes.
- Root-cause hypothesis: transient proxy read backlog at us-west-2 combined with recent autoscaler policy reduction on the dedicated pool for DH-47821. Under sustained small bursts KV cache miss amplification increased per-request latency, which surfaced as extended silent windows and connection timeouts at the gateway.
- Actions taken:
  * Increased proxy_read_timeout and connection keepalives for the route (monitoring in place).
  * Added two temporary instances and raised concurrency cap for DH-47821.
  * Rolling audit of autoscaler policy across dedicated pools (Evelyn to lead).
  * Customer guidance: short-term polling fallback and client keepalive recommendations shared.
- Outstanding asks / exec decisions required:
  1) Approve a $25K one-time credit for HelioHealth to cover outage impact (requested by their operations lead). They are a mid-market, high-touch customer.
  2) Approve priority engineering support (2 wks) for autoscaler policy tuning and KV cache instrumentation (timeboxed).

Metrics & links: INF-9213 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9213) — includes logs, graphs, and post-mortem draft.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v2.pdf, helio_live_logs_0406.zip
